chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn Ibrahim, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
“There is no problem with a garment whose warp, buttons, and trim are silk; rather, what is disliked for men is plain silk.”
Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: And one does not perform salat (prayer) in al-fanak or al-sammur, and salat (prayer) is not valid in the furs of that whose meat is not eaten.

key_terms.أَوْبَارِ: fur or hair used in garments
key_terms.سَدَاهُ: the warp threads of the garment
key_terms.عَلَمُهُ: its trim, edging, or decorative marking
key_terms.ٱلثَّوْبِ: garment or clothing being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity is under discussion
key_terms.ٱلْحَرِيرُ ٱلْبُهْمُ: plain pure silk without mixture or distinction

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for men to wear garments with some silk, and can salat (prayer) be performed in animal furs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding garments used in salat (prayer), clarifying that a garment containing some silk in its warp, buttons, or trim is not problematic. It further states that what is disapproved for men is plain silk, and adds that salat (prayer) is not valid in the fur of animals whose meat is not lawful to eat.
